pageCache.pageTitle: Infiniti School - SEMH School in Sittingbourne, Kent.
pageCache.text:
Infiniti School SEMH
Welcome to Infiniti School - We are an Ofsted rated "GOOD" school.
Introduction to Infiniti School
We are an independent SEMH Secondary School for individuals aged 11-18. We cater for students individual needs and provide an enriching education that allows them to reach their full potential.
Here's a short video to show you what we are all about!
Who we are:
Idyllic location
Our school is based in an idyllic location on an amazing site in Doddington. Built in 1867, the school buildings and grounds are an ideal setting for students to learn.
SEMH school
At Infiniti School, we can welcome up to 32 students in years 7 to post-16, who have special educational needs where their primary need is for Social, Emotional or Mental Health difficulties.
Inclusive
We aim to provide an outstanding education for students with special educational needs which engages and excites them now, as well as prepares them for the rest of their lives.
Our Values
Engagement
There are no limits to our curiosity, creativity and commitment to life skills, achievements and opportunities. Challenges are tackled with determination, balance and resilience. We take pride in making responsible choices in and outside school.
Ownership
We can achieve anything if we try our best, own our behaviour and health and learn from our mistakes. Every day is a new day with fresh challenges taken on in a spirit of honesty, fairness, trust, respect, fun and good humour.
Compassion
We celebrate our own individuality and the diversity of all in our school and the wider community and beyond. Our self-respect means we express tolerance of others and kindness and inclusion to all in a spirit of openness, fairness and friendship.
Our curriculum
We are incredibly proud to offer a broad and balanced curriculum including a range of subjects that are highly differentiated to enable students to re-engage with learning. Find out more about what subjects we have to offer, and how our curriculum has been developed to allow each student to thrive.
Parent Testimonials
Infiniti has changed my son’s outlook on learning. He has made so much progress and his confidence is amazing! I can’t thank everyone enough for what they have done for my son.
Excellent, supportive, focus on children's wellbeing so they can learn.
You have really turned things around for our son!!
I am really pleased with how the school supports my son, and adapts things when needed. Brilliant school & staff.
As a family, we have so much to thank the school for and I am forever grateful to the staff for their kindness during the years my son attended the school.
Join Us:
Vacancies
Our Staff
Our Governors

OAA (Outdoor Adventurous Activities)
OAA is all about taking students outside their comfort zone to learn new skills in an off-site location. Skills are built up gradually over a few weeks, giving students a real chance to improve, build confidence, and see their own progress week on week.
Activities
Students take part in a range of outdoor and adventurous activities, including:
Snowboarding
Bouldering
Mountain Biking
Forest School
Watersports
Fishing with Trailblazers
Alongside these activities, we offer a fishing provision through Trailblazers. Students learn how to fish, while developing patience and experiencing the genuine reward of a successful catch — skills and qualities that extend well beyond the riverbank.
Horse riding with Deepdene Stables
We also run a horse riding and education provision with Deepdene Stables, where students learn how to ride and how to properly care for a horse — combining a physical skill with the responsibility of looking after another living creature.

Safeguarding
Safeguarding at Infiniti School
Safeguarding and promoting the welfare of our students is at the heart of everything we do. Every member of staff, governor and volunteer at Infiniti School shares responsibility for keeping our students safe, and we are committed to creating a calm, secure environment where every young person can thrive.
Our approach
We follow the statutory guidance set out in Keeping Children Safe in Education and work closely with the Kent Safeguarding Children Multi-Agency Partnership, local authorities, and other agencies to protect the welfare of every student in our care. Our full approach is set out in our Child Protection and Safeguarding Policy available in our Policies section.
Our Designated Safeguarding Lead
Our Designated Safeguarding Lead (DSL) has overall responsibility for safeguarding at Infiniti School and is supported by a team of Deputy DSLs across the school day.
If you have any concern about the safety or welfare of a child, please contact the DSL directly using the details above, or speak to any member of staff, who will act promptly.
If you're worried about a child
If you believe a child is in immediate danger, please call 999.
If you have a safeguarding concern that is not an emergency, you can also contact:
Kent Children's Social Care: [phone number]
NSPCC Helpline: 0808 800 5000
Keeping our students safe online
We take online safety seriously and have a dedicated [Online Safety Policy](LINK TO CURRENT PDF) covering how we support students to stay safe online, both in school and at home. Guidance for parents on supporting safe internet use at home is available from UK Safer Internet Centre and CEOP.
Related policies
All avaliable on our Policies page

Art
Art at Infiniti encourages students to express and engage with their creativity, building skills and making wider connections to the world around them.
A wide range of materials and techniques
We work with a broad range of materials and techniques, giving students the chance to explore clay, paint, batik, printing, collage materials, stop animation and much more. Students also explore a wide range of topics and engage with the work of other artists, broadening their creative influences alongside their own practice.
Qualification pathway
Supporting every student
We believe every student can benefit from creative endeavour, whatever stage they're at in their learning — Art is taught and adapted to make sure that's true for everyone, not just those who already see themselves as "good at art."

English
At Key Stage 3, English is about closing gaps and building confidence — helping every student become a more capable, more assured reader and writer. At Key Stage 4, the focus shifts towards practical skills that students can carry with them into life, learning and work beyond school.
Key Stage 3
Our KS3 programme blends the National Curriculum with Functional Skills standards, so every student is working on what they actually need — across reading, writing, grammar and spoken English. Alongside regular lessons, students take part in focused reading intervention sessions, giving them extra time to build a genuine love of reading across a range of genres, and to talk through the ideas and themes they come across.
Students also use Bedrock Learning, an online programme that builds vocabulary and reading comprehension through short, regular sessions — helping students understand more of what they read, and use richer language in their own writing.
Key Stage 4 — three routes, matched to the student
Not every student is ready for the same qualification at the same time, so we offer three pathways:
By the end of Key Stage 4, students will be able to:

Humanities
Humanities at Infiniti covers a broad spectrum of subject areas — most closely associated with History, Geography and Religious Studies. It's crucial for all learners to become well-rounded, culturally responsive global citizens who can understand and question the world around them, and their place in it. Our aim is to encourage students to explore and understand that world for themselves.
Learning that builds over time
Lessons are designed to provide variety, opportunities for consolidation, and enough challenge to keep students interested and progressing. Students revisit topics several times throughout their school career, reinforcing and solidifying key information with each return, while progressing from simple ideas to more complex ones — applying what they learned early on to new objectives later.
Learning beyond the classroom
We use visits to relevant places of interest to complement classroom learning, helping bring topics to life and giving students a real-world connection to what they're studying.

Maths
Every student's maths learning starts from the National Curriculum, but is then shaped around them — reflecting the targets in their Annual Review or Education, Health and Care Plan. For some students this means a fully personalised timetable built around specific needs. Lessons are designed to be meaningful and differentiated for every ability level, using visual learning material, tasks broken into small, achievable steps, and plenty of practical, hands-on and interactive work.
Key Stage 3
Our KS3 programme focuses on closing gaps and building confidence — giving students the problem-solving skills and self-belief to keep progressing. It blends the National Curriculum with Functional Skills standards across number, algebra, data handling, geometry, and ratio and proportion. Students who need extra support also access focused 1:1 intervention sessions, working through individualised tasks at their own pace.
Key Stage 4 — two routes, matched to the student
By the end of Key Stage 4, students will be able to:

PE
At Key Stage 3, PE focuses on developing, refining and applying core skills across different practical conditions, alongside building a basic understanding of sporting terminology, rules and regulations. At Key Stage 4, students continue to develop and refine those same core skills in greater detail, while building a deeper understanding of game rules, different roles within sports, and the ability to review their own performance.
Key Stage 3
The KS3 programme incorporates areas of the National Curriculum to meet the needs of the individual, covering a wide range of sports and games to build basic and core skills.
Sports and activities
Across their PE lessons, students take part in a wide range of sports and activities, including:
Football
Basketball
Cricket
Tag Rugby
Gymnastics
Lacrosse
Handball
Swimming
Rounders
Tennis
Badminton
Pickleball
Assessment — AQA Unit Awards
Students are assessed through AQA Unit Awards, a unitised programme of non-examined assessments that lets students achieve at Pre-Entry Level, Entry Level, and Level 1, 2 or 3 — without the need for formal exams.
Qualification pathway
At Key Stage 4, students also have the opportunity to work towards an NCFE Level 1 Certificate in Sport — a chance to expand their knowledge of the sporting landscape, both through their own personal performance and the wider sporting industry and the opportunities it can offer. This is achieved through coursework across a range of units, alongside practical assessment.
By the end of Key Stage 4, students will be able to:

PSHE
In PSHE (Personal, Social, Health and Economic education), our intention is to help students develop the knowledge, skills and attributes they need to manage their lives, now and in the future — staying healthy, safe, and prepared for life and work in modern Britain.
Mental health and wellbeing at the centre
We place real importance on mental health and wellbeing, making sure students are well-prepared for the challenges ahead of them. We aim to equip students with the knowledge and confidence to take care of themselves, and to know how to get support if a problem arises — building the resilience and personal qualities that help students become successful, productive members of society.
Staying safe online and offline
In a world where so much of life happens both on and offline, we aim to give students the skills to stay safe and healthy in both — helping them manage their digital and real-world lives in a positive way.
A curriculum that reflects our students
Our school has an ethnically diverse population, and many students have specific needs or come from disadvantaged backgrounds. We make sure the timing and delivery of PSHE sessions reflect and respect the backgrounds and ethnicity of our students, so every topic is taught sensitively and relevantly.
Our curriculum is built around three strands:

Science
Our science curriculum is designed to give every student the best possible chance of leaving with a qualification by the end of Year 11, while building a broad, practical appreciation of the science and technology they'll rely on in adult life. We currently work towards AQA Certificates or GCSE in Science.
What we cover
We teach six core topics, each building on the last:
The Human Body
The Environment
Chemistry in Our World
Elements, Mixtures and Compounds
Energy and Forces
Electricity and Magnetism
A spiral curriculum
Rather than covering a topic once and moving on, our spiral curriculum revisits each area year after year — so knowledge and understanding build steadily over time, rather than needing to be relearned from scratch.
Key Stage 4 — matched to the student
Our overarching aim is to prepare students for independent life in a world that relies more and more on a broad understanding of science and technology. Where appropriate, students take formal exams. Where that's not the right fit, they instead have many opportunities to practise experimental and research skills, building a sound foundation of scientific knowledge either way.
Wherever possible, we bring learning to life through doing, not just reading about it — for example, students learn the process of photosynthesis first-hand by tending crops in the school allotment, rather than only studying it on paper.
By the end of Key Stage 4, students will have developed:

Work Experience
Students in Year 10 and above are offered the opportunity to gain direct work experience during their studies — a chance to build real-world skills and confidence outside the classroom.
Tailored to the student
Placements can be tailored to each student, drawing on local connections and other businesses affiliated with the school, so students get experience that's relevant to their own interests and goals.
Group work experience
We also offer group work experience, a more accessible option for students who benefit from taking part alongside their peers rather than in a one-to-one placement.
Animal Care
Students interested in tending to animals are welcome to pick Animal Care as an additional subject, gaining direct, hands-on experience at Creepy Claws.
What students do
Students get involved in the day-to-day care of the animals, including:
It's a chance for students to build responsibility and practical animal-care skills while learning about a genuinely wide range of species.
Cleaning
Multitrades
Students interested in developing a trade are welcome to travel to Goldwyn School to hone their craft across a range of different trades — from bricklaying to mechanics.
Why it matters
Multitrades gives students hands-on exposure to real trade skills and working environments, helping them explore practical career paths and build confidence in a hands-on, vocational setting.

pageCache.pageTitle: Work With Us | Infiniti School, Sittingbourne.
pageCache.text:
Would you like to work with us?
We are always keen to hear from teachers and support staff who are interested in coming to work at Infiniti School. For an informal chat, or to find out more, please email us or call us on 01795 886687.
Any job listings will be on our Kent Teach page, https://www.kent-teach.com/School/Directory/Details.aspx?SchoolId=2902

Personal Development
Personal Development is a chance for students to explore what makes them who they are. Students create projects based on their own personal interests, experiment with new forms of craft, and work towards their own personal aspirations.
A therapeutic environment
All of this takes place in a therapeutic environment, where students can relax and settle — making sure their wellbeing is in the right place before moving into their next lessons.
Life Skills
Life Skills equips students with the practical, everyday knowledge they need to navigate independence with confidence. From buying a train ticket to managing a budget, students build the kind of real-world competence that isn't always taught in a traditional classroom.
Employability
Employability helps students understand the world of work and start preparing for it with purpose. Whether they're years away from their first job or ready to start applying, students leave with practical tools and a clearer sense of direction.

Food Technology
Our main aim is for every student to be able to plan, prepare and cook meals for themselves and others — building the practical confidence they'll need for independent living.
Weekly, hands-on cooking
Every week, students get the chance to cook, creating a wide range of different dishes over the course of the year. Support is tailored to each student, helping them succeed now while working towards greater independence at their own pace.
Safety first, adapted to the individual
Health and safety is a top priority in every lesson. Each student's individual needs are taken into account, with learning adapted so every student can take part safely and successfully.
Qualification pathway
Students will learn to:

ICT
ICT equips students with the digital skills and understanding they'll need for everyday life, further study and future work — from the basics of how a computer works through to staying safe online.
Key Stage 3
Students begin by learning the basic hardware and software of a computer, before developing skills across key application software — including word processing, presentation software and visual communication tools. They also get to experiment with digital photography, giving them the chance to use technology in a fun, creative way.
Key Stage 4
At Key Stage 4, students build on the skills introduced at KS3, while studying cybersecurity in more detail — helping them understand how to safeguard themselves online in adult life. Students can gain a Functional Skills qualification as soon as they're ready, starting at Entry Level 3 and progressing through Level 1 and Level 2. Students who excel in ICT have the opportunity to move on to further qualifications.
Learning online
All students have their own Google Classroom account, where teachers can set and manage work online — helping build the kind of digital organisation and independence students will rely on beyond school.
Qualification pathway
